title: Extruded rows
what: Exactly the locked content: the head, the title and rows 01-06, word for word, nothing added. The form adds only physical parts: a base plate with edge thickness and corner marks, five raised tiles with visible side faces, and one empty recessed socket with an orange rim for row 06.
why: The Standard is shown as something assembled piece by piece: each rule, skill or scenario is a solid part that someone brought and set into the plate. The empty socket says the set is not finished and there is a slot shaped for your contribution, which is the resource's whole ask (open, community-built, a place for you).
how: Real CSS 3D in one preserve-3d context: the plate (black top with a cut-out, bottom and left edge faces) leans back, tiles stand 14px above it with lit bottom and shaded left faces, the socket is a hole with two inner walls and a floor 14px down where row 06's text sits; neutral tone gradients for volume, 1px hairlines, orange only on row 06. On load the plate settles, the tiles rise up through it one by one, their text writes in and the socket rim draws last (about 1.1s); the pointer tilts the plate slightly, and hovering or focusing row 06 lifts its floor a little and writes the dashed line solid. Reduced motion shows the final state with no tilt; under 700px the plate lies flat as a readable list with a 2px tile edge and a full-width 44px+ tap target on row 06.
